title: Resolve-by-reference pinning: stability contract and client semantics
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Define and implement a deterministic, user-friendly pin-by-reference contract across Redwood API and SDKs. The feature must allow customers to pin models by three primary forms: human-friendly tags (e.g., 'stable', 'latest'), semver-like versions (e.g., 'v1.4.2'), and opaque build identifiers/commit hashes (e.g., 'd4c3b2a'). This ticket codifies the resolution order, compatibility guarantees, fallback semantics, and client-side behaviors (caching, TTL, verification) to avoid accidental regressions during rollouts or when a tag moves to a different underlying artifact.
acceptance_criteria: API defines unambiguous semantics for pin types: tag, semver, commit-hash and a documented resolution precedence
SDKs (Python/Node/Go) expose a stable Pin class with helper methods: resolve(), verify_stability(), and explain_resolution()
Server-side resolver supports: exact-match hash resolution, semver range interpretation, tag->latest mapping, and deterministic tie-breaking when multiple model variants match
Resolution events are recorded to audit logs with: request_id, resolved_model_id, resolution_path (e.g., tag->semver->hash), and timestamp
Backward-compatible behavior: existing API calls without pins continue to use the current default model selection behavior
End-to-end tests verifying fallback flows (e.g., tag points to deleted model; semver range has no match) return clear 4xx/5xx codes with actionable errors
Documentation and migration guide published and linked from SDK release notes
decisions: Pin precedence: explicit commit-hash > exact semver match > semver range (highest stable patch) > tag mapping
Tags are mutable references and must be treated as first-class moving pointers; SDKs will provide optional "verify_stability()" hooks to guard against accidental tag drift

Semver support will be limited to the subset we control: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with optional range selector syntax (e.g., ^1.3, ~2.0). We will not implement full npm-style semver parsing to reduce complexity

When a tag resolves to multiple model artifacts (cross-region or variant builds), resolver picks the artifact matching the request's route policy (region/latency tiers), with a deterministic stable fallback ordering
We will return a 409 Conflict when a pin cannot be resolved unambiguously within the request constraints rather than silently selecting a variant
implementation_notes: Server: add resolver endpoint /v1/models/resolve that accepts {pin_type, pin_value, constraints} and returns {resolved_model_id, provenance_chain}
Server: emit resolution audit event to infra-logs topic; include fields for TTL, variant_hash, and compatibility_flags
SDK: add Pin utility to wind up resolution and allow local caching with configurable TTL (default 60s); TTL must be lower than server-side tag TTL
SDK: include explain_resolution() that humanizes provenance_chain for logs and error messages
Migration: introduce beta flag within API (pinning=beta) to gate rollout and collect usage telemetry
Edge-case: if semver range resolves to an experimental/quantized build, tag should include stability label and SDK verify_stability() must warn by default
test_plan: Unit tests for resolver: exact-hash, semver-exact, semver-range, tag->latest, tag deletion
Integration tests: SDK resolve() against local mock resolver and staging control plane to ensure consistent TTL behavior
Chaos test: concurrent tag updates while resolving to confirm deterministic tie-breaker and no 500s
Security test: ensure audit events do not leak model internals beyond model_id and provenance hash
Performance test: measure added latency for resolve call (target < 2ms p95 in cache hit path, < 15ms cold)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (alpha): internal SDKs and infra use only. Enable feature flag for small subset of internal tenants (2 teams)
Phase 2 (beta): expose to customers with pinning=beta header; collect opt-in telemetry and support requests
Phase 3 (GA): promote to default; update docs and SDK default TTLs; deprecate old experimental pin endpoints
Rollback: server maintains previous resolution path for 72 hours and we can toggle tag immutability to force previous mapping
linked_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/856 - UI: model pin selector and resolution inspector
comments: 2025-02-14 Sofia Martinez: Initial scoping write-up. Goal is to make pin-by-reference explicit and avoid silent model swaps that cause regressions. Added preliminary acceptance criteria.

2025-02-18 Eric Liu: Pushed prototype resolver for semver exact and hash matching to runtime branch feature/resolve-pin. Observed cache invalidation edge-case when tags flip rapidly — added TTL to design notes.
2025-02-21 Hannah Cho (PM): Please make sure console UX surfaces the provenance_chain and an easy 'lock to commit' action. Customers want one-click immutability for a pinned route.

2025-02-25 Code Review (runtime): @james-k flagged that semver-range selection may need to consider quantization flags; recommended adding compatibility flags to model metadata. Action: add compatibility_flags to provenance_chain (Eric)
2025-02-28 Design review: @Maya-R gave feedback on explain_resolution() wording. Updated messages to avoid jargon for RFC-3987 style semver ranges. Also requested example strings for SDK logs.

2025-03-01 QA: Added integration tests for tag deletion fallback. Observed server returns 500 on simultaneous delete+resolve — root cause is race in tag index; mitigation: serializable update path (PR: runtime#2005)
2025-03-02 Release lead (Anil Patel): Recommend gating GA behind security review and adding an audit retention flag. Marking ticket In Review pending security sign-off and console PR approvals.
